checks: Inversion X=Y/(1−Y) changes the original density 1/(1+X) to 1/(1−Y) on the entire interval [0,1/2].

A compact convex body with positive Lebesgue volume is full-dimensional. The support of its projected volume is the entire projection. Each interior projection value has an interior preimage by interpolating an interior point with a point beyond that value.

Section containment and Brunn–Minkowski give a concave positive r-th root on the interior of the projection. Continuity upgrades almost-everywhere agreement with the claimed density root to pointwise agreement, contradicting the strictly positive second derivative for every finite r≥1.

For the three fixed labels the midpoint section inequality compares roots after canceling the common factor. Strict convexity of t^(−1/r) and unequal positive endpoint denominators give the opposite strict inequality for every finite r≥1.
The middle upper bound sD and endpoint lower bounds sν/D give D^(2/r) at least the mean of the endpoint roots. AM–GM and raising to r/2 give [e(2−e)]^(−1/4), diverging as e tends to zero.
